This document covers frequently asked questions and known issues when using **catviz**.

---

## Installation & Loading

**Q: I get "there is no package called 'catviz'"**

Install from GitHub until CRAN release:
```r
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("VictorKilanko/catviz")
```

**Q: `devtools::load_all()` works but `library(catviz)` doesn't find my functions**

Run `devtools::install()` in the catviz project directory first. `load_all()` only
works in the development environment; `install()` makes the package available to
`library()`.

---

## cat_spec() issues

**Q: Error "not all vars are in names(data)"**

Make sure the column names you pass to `cat_spec()` exactly match your data frame.
Column names are case-sensitive.

```r
# Wrong:
cat_spec(df, id="Hospital_ID", ...)   # if column is actually "hospital_id"

# Right:
cat_spec(df, id="hospital_id", ...)
```

**Q: My `g` column has `NA` instead of `Inf` for never-treated units**

Replace `NA` with `Inf` before calling `cat_spec()`:
```r
df$g[is.na(df$g)] <- Inf
```
Or add `NA` to `never_treated_values`:
```r
cat_spec(df, ..., never_treated_values = c(0, Inf, NA))
```

**Q: `cat_spec()` assigns everything to "Unclassified" node**

This usually means `g` is a character column. Convert it to numeric:
```r
df$g <- as.numeric(df$g)
```
Or make sure your `g` values are comparable to `.time` values
(both should be numeric years or both dates).

**Q: I don't have a subgroup variable — can I still use catviz?**

Yes. Simply omit the `subgroup` argument:
```r
spec <- cat_spec(df, id="id", time="year", g="g")   # pure CSDiD
```
`cat_plot_tree()` will automatically use the CSDiD or 2×2 DiD layout.

---

## cat_label() issues

**Q: cat_label() only assigns letters A, B for two cohorts but I have more**

Make sure your `g` column is numeric (not character). The function sorts
finite g values to assign letters chronologically.

**Q: Never-treated units get letter "B" but I expected "E"**

The last letter in the sequence always goes to never-treated. With N treated
cohorts, never-treated gets letter N+1. So with 1 treated cohort, NT gets "B";
with 4, it gets "E". This is by design.

---

## cat_plot_tree() / plot issues

**Q: "Scale for fill is already present" warning with grayscale**

This warning is harmless — it just means the grayscale palette is replacing
the default color palette. Your plot will be correct.

**Q: Nodes are overlapping or cut off**

Try adjusting the saved figure width and height:
```r
cat_save_png(p, "tree.png", width=18, height=10, dpi=300)
```
Or use `ggsave()` directly:
```r
ggplot2::ggsave("tree.png", p, width=20, height=12, dpi=300)
```

**Q: "No treated cohorts detected" error**

This means all your `g` values are in `never_treated_values`. Check that:
1. Your `g` column has finite values for treated units
2. `never_treated_values` is correctly set (default: `c(0, Inf)`)

**Q: "2×2 DID requires exactly one treated group" error**

`cat_plot_did()` requires exactly one unique finite `g` value. If you have
multiple cohorts, use `cat_plot_csdid()` or let `cat_plot_tree()` auto-select.

---

## cat_diag() issues

**Q: DR-DDD diagnostic error: "subgroup variable required"**

The DR-DDD diagnostic needs a binary subgroup variable. Make sure you passed
`subgroup = "your_col"` to `cat_spec()`.

**Q: The pretrend plot is empty / has no lines**

The `pre_window` argument controls which event times are included. If your
data has a short pre-period, adjust accordingly:
```r
cat_diag(spec, outcome="y", method="csdid", pre_window=-3:-1)
```

**Q: "Never-treated" has no observations in the diagnostic**

If all observations with `.NT == 1` fall outside `pre_window`, the control
line won't appear. Check your time variable and never-treated classification.

---

## cat_balance_table() issues

**Q: Error in `dplyr::group_by(g)`: undefined column**

Make sure all covariate names match columns in your data:
```r
names(spec$data)   # check available columns
cat_balance_table(spec, covariates=c("income","age"))  # must be in data
```

**Q: SMD values are very large (>5)**

This can happen if a covariate has near-zero variance within one group.
Check for degenerate variables (constants, all-NA, etc.).

---

## CRAN submission

**Q: Which folder do I submit to CRAN?**

Submit the `CRAN/catviz/` folder. That is the complete R package directory.
Go to `https://cran.r-project.org/submit.html`, upload the `.tar.gz` file
you create with:
```r
devtools::build("CRAN/catviz")
# This creates catviz_0.1.0.tar.gz — upload that file
```

**Q: R CMD check gives NOTE about "no visible binding for global variable"**

This is a common note from rlang's non-standard evaluation. Add to your
function using `.data[[var]]` instead of bare variable names, or suppress
with `utils::globalVariables()`. The CRAN team typically accepts packages
with 0 errors, 0 warnings, and a small number of notes.

**Q: R CMD check gives WARNING "no documentation for..."**

Run `devtools::document()` to regenerate man/ files from roxygen comments
before checking. Then re-run `devtools::check()`.

---

## General tips

| Symptom | First thing to check |
|---------|---------------------|
| All nodes "Unclassified" | `g` column is character, not numeric |
| NT nodes missing from plot | `g == 0` not in `never_treated_values` |
| Letters wrong | `g` column has ties or unexpected values |
| Plot too crowded | Too many cohorts — increase `width` in `ggsave()` |
| Pretrend plot empty | `pre_window` doesn't match event times in data |
| Balance SMD = NaN | Covariate is constant or all-NA in a group |
